themes.title: Far-right parties exploit migration crises for political gain
themes.blurb: Right-wing and far-right parties across Europe are leveraging the recent migration crisis in Ceuta to push for stricter border controls and anti-immigration policies. This theme is particularly strong in Spain, Italy, and Germany, where parties like Vox, Fratelli d'Italia, Lega, and AfD are framing the crisis as a national security threat and demanding tougher government action.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Demands investigation into Spain's PM for alleged treason over Ceuta migrant crisis, boycotts meetings on migrant minors redistribution, and calls for stricter border controls.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italy suspends Schengen rules with Spain over Ceuta migrant influx, escalating diplomatic tensions and justifying border controls as a security measure.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: Uses migration issues to push for stricter border policies and criticize the government's handling of immigration, aligning with broader far-right narratives.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: Proposes using the Royal Navy to block small boat crossings in the Channel, echoing far-right anti-immigration rhetoric.

themes.title: Right-wing leaders rally behind restrictive birthright citizenship policies

themes.title: Right-wing governments target social programs amid fiscal debates
themes.blurb: Right-wing governments in the U.S., Argentina, and Hungary are pushing for significant cuts to social programs, framing these measures as necessary for fiscal responsibility. This includes reductions in healthcare, education, and welfare programs, often sparking public backlash and internal government conflicts.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Proposes deregulating Head Start programs and cutting homelessness funding, aiming to reduce federal spending on social programs.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Cuts to healthcare coverage and social programs have led to public backlash, with over 1.25 million Argentinians losing private health coverage.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza
countries.note: Implements austerity measures, including cuts to public media funding and energy subsidies, amid economic crises.
